title: The cutover rehearsal covers 1 of 5 mainnet dispatcher swaps and is not re-targetable to the other classes: `REHEARSAL_SWAP_INDEX` reads like a knob but the helper hard-codes the index-1 6-decimal Uniboost shape, so index 4 — the 18-decimal prime with the BPT custody shift — stays entirely unrehearsed
fingerprintNote: Accepted VERBATIM as supplied by dedup. NOT recomputed by finding-manager. The fingerprint is the only collision-proof key for this record; the label L-xx/Q-xx is run-scoped and collides with run-21 and run-26 labels on this same entry point.
description: DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol performs the swap on five indices — 1, 2, 3 (Uniboost, USDC 6dp), 4 (BalancerPoolerV2, USDS 18dp) and 7 (NudgeRatchet) — with pull/setDispatcher/setHook/replaceDispatcher call sites at :1300/:1341/:1342/:1363, :1456/:1519/:1520/:1528 and :1584/:1623/:1624/:1632. Phase 7.6 mirrors exactly one, on index 1. Indices 2 and 3 are genuine duplicates and cost nothing. Index 7's two distinguishing claims are honestly pinned by static assertions (hookTypeId, ratio == 100), both of which execute and pass. Index 4 has NO local mirror of any kind, and it is the index that differs most: its mainnet swap carries a BPT custody transfer old -> new governed by a five-clause safety doctrine and a resume guard (:1385-1420), and its hook `scale` is 1 rather than 1e12 because the prime is 18-decimal USDS. The local rehearsal only ever exercises the 6-decimal branch, so any defect class that manifests only on an 18-decimal prime is definitionally out of reach. Crucially the helper is NOT re-targetable despite appearances: `REHEARSAL_SWAP_INDEX` (:225) looks like a knob, but `_rehearseDispatcherSwap` constructs the replacement as a `Uniboost` (:1805), asserts `rewardToken.decimals() == 6` (:1818), and asserts `require(price < 1e12, "index price is not 6-decimal-shaped")` (:1846) — which would FAIL outright at index 4, where the registered price is 10 * 10**18. Changing the constant alone therefore breaks the run. Note also that `price < 1e12` is a magnitude heuristic with no mainnet counterpart.
impact: The class of defect the local chain can catch is 'a 6-decimal Uniboost swap went wrong', not 'a cutover swap went wrong'. The BPT custody shift — the single highest-value movement in the whole cutover — and the 18-decimal-prime hook-scale interaction remain rehearsed nowhere. The ordering property itself IS class-independent and is genuinely gated, so this narrows the fix's reach rather than negating it.
attackPath: 1. Not an attack path — a miss path, and a demonstrated rather than hypothetical one.
2. A cutover defect specific to index 4 is introduced or already present in DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol.
3. `npm run dev` rehearses index 1 only, passes green, and the ordering assertions all hold.

4. The index-4 defect reaches the mainnet cutover unrehearsed. This has ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE: ledger 85d794b386b15b20 (acknowledged Medium, entryPoint dispatcher-replace-sky-pooler) — 'Sky-pooler cutover leaves index-4 unmintable: newPooler._minter never set to NFTMinterV2, mint(4) reverts' — is a real index-4 cutover defect that shipped, at precisely the index this finding shows is rehearsed nowhere.
recommendation: Two options, in preference order. (a) Add a second rehearsal on index 4 in a follow-on story: swap BalancerPoolerV2 with the BPT custody shift mirrored (old.withdrawBPT(new) with the destination asserted, then replaceDispatcher(4)), which exercises the 18-decimal prime, `scale == 1`, and the highest-value movement in the cutover. (b) At minimum, make the existing helper honestly index-1-only: rename `REHEARSAL_SWAP_INDEX` to something that does not read as a knob, or replace the hard-coded `price < 1e12` with a decimals-derived bound (`price < 10 ** (uint256(IERC20Metadata(prime).decimals()) + 6)` or equivalent) and gate the `decimals() == 6` assertion on the dispatcher class. Either way, add a comment stating explicitly which mainnet indices are and are not mirrored, so the coverage claim is not over-read.
severityRationale: Not High: no asset is reachable, nothing is stealable, and the artifact is a local rehearsal. Not Medium either, and this is the load-bearing judgement of the run: C4 Medium wants the protocol's function or availability impacted, or value leaked under stated assumptions. This finding impacts the coverage of a TEST, not the protocol. A rehearsal gap does not itself cause loss; it removes one gate that would have caught a loss caused by something else — and the something else that already got through is filed and acknowledged in its own right (85d794b3), where its severity properly lives. Counting the same escaped defect a second time here, on the rehearsal artifact, would double-book it and inflate the report. It is nonetheless a real Low rather than QA, on two independent grounds: the unmirrored index carries the highest-value movement in the whole cutover (a BPT custody transfer) and a different decimal class, so the gap is not a duplicate of the covered case; and the parameterised-LOOKING constant actively invites a false belief that re-targeting is cheap, which is a trap rather than a mere absence.
severityRationaleAsProposed: Proposed Low. Rehearsal-coverage defect on a local-only script: no on-chain asset is at risk and no mainnet behaviour changes. It is a real Low rather than QA because the unrehearsed index is the one carrying the highest-value movement in the cutover (a BPT custody transfer) and a different decimal class, and because the parameterised-looking constant invites a future operator to believe re-targeting is a one-line change when it is not.

classification.assetImpact: None directly. Local-only script, mock tokens, chain 31337. No mainnet behaviour changes and no on-chain asset is reachable.
classification.whatActuallyBreaks: The class of defect the local chain can catch is narrower than it appears. Phase 7.6 mirrors exactly one of the five mainnet dispatcher swaps (index 1, Uniboost, 6-decimal USDC). Indices 2 and 3 are genuine duplicates and cost nothing; index 7's two distinguishing claims are honestly pinned by executing static assertions. Index 4 has no local mirror of any kind, and it is the index that differs most: an 18-decimal USDS prime (hook `scale == 1` rather than `1e12`) and a BPT custody transfer old->new governed by a five-clause safety doctrine plus a resume guard. Any defect class that manifests only on an 18-decimal prime, or only in the BPT custody shift, is definitionally out of the local rehearsal's reach.
classification.whatAnOperatorGainsOrLoses: A future operator reading `REHEARSAL_SWAP_INDEX` (:225) reasonably believes re-targeting the rehearsal is a one-line change. It is not: `_rehearseDispatcherSwap` constructs the replacement as a `Uniboost` (:1805), asserts `rewardToken.decimals() == 6` (:1818), and asserts `require(price < 1e12, "index price is not 6-decimal-shaped")` (:1846) — the last of which fails outright at index 4, where the registered price is 10 * 10**18. So the knob-shaped constant buys a broken run, not extra coverage. `price < 1e12` is additionally a magnitude heuristic with no mainnet counterpart.
attackPath: 1. Not an attack path — a miss path, and a demonstrated rather than hypothetical one.
2. A cutover defect specific to index 4 is introduced or already present in DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol.
3. `npm run dev` rehearses index 1 only, passes green, and the ordering assertions all hold.

4. The index-4 defect reaches the mainnet cutover unrehearsed. This has ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE: ledger 85d794b386b15b20 (acknowledged Medium, entryPoint dispatcher-replace-sky-pooler) — 'Sky-pooler cutover leaves index-4 unmintable: newPooler._minter never set to NFTMinterV2, mint(4) reverts' — is a real index-4 cutover defect that shipped, at precisely the index this finding shows is rehearsed nowhere.
classification.likelihood: The coverage gap itself is certain and permanent until an index-4 mirror is written. The likelihood that it *costs* something is evidenced, not speculative — one index-4 cutover defect has already shipped. Weighed down, though, by the fact that the defect which escaped is already separately filed and acknowledged, so this entry is not the only thing standing between that class of bug and the operator.
classification.assumptions: That the promotion-ready mainnet cutover will in fact execute the index-4 swap including the BPT custody transfer, as DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:1456/:1519/:1520/:1528 and the :1385-1420 resume guard indicate.
classification.externalRequirements: A future index-4-specific defect must exist for the gap to bite again. The gap alone changes nothing on chain.

escalationTrigger: Raise to MEDIUM if ANY of the following becomes true: (a) the index-4 mainnet swap — including the BPT custody transfer old->new — is scheduled for broadcast while it remains rehearsed NOWHERE (no local mirror, no fork rehearsal in the promotion-ready entry point, no Foundry unit test covering the custody shift), because at that point this gap is the sole missing gate on the highest-value movement in the cutover; or (b) a SECOND index-4-specific cutover defect is discovered, which would establish the miss as recurring rather than a single incident; or (c) the BPT custody transfer is found to be non-recoverable once mis-executed (no owner-side rescue path), since an unrehearsed irreversible high-value movement is an availability/value question, not a coverage question. Absent all three, Low is the honest label.
law3: No owner-malice vector. The knob-that-is-not-a-knob is arguably an operational trap for a future operator, but it fails loudly (the run breaks) rather than silently enabling anything, so it is not a footgun in the Law-3 sense either.

poc.reason: C4 requires a coded PoC for High/Medium only. Severity here is low.

labelCollisionWarning: Run-scoped label only. On entry point `dev` the ledger already holds a run-21 L-02 and/or a run-26 L-02 under different fingerprints. Never key any artifact, carryover copy or ledger operation on this label; key on fingerprint 6af1ae30ed82… (or issueId pps27l2).
borderlineNote: FLAGGED FOR HUMAN. This is the one record in the run where Low vs Medium is a genuine judgement call rather than a comfortable fit. The Medium case: an index-4 cutover defect has demonstrably already shipped, the unmirrored leg carries the cutover's highest-value movement, and the coverage claim is over-readable. The Low case (adopted): the artifact is a local test, the escaped defect is separately filed at its own severity, and elevating a test-coverage gap to Medium on the strength of a bug that is already booked would double-count it. Recorded so the choice is visible.

Run-26's recommendation said in terms 'One index is sufficient to make the ordering executable and therefore regression-testable' and left the index unspecified; the implementation did exactly that.
